description: Verifies the seal of a solution. Short form, which needs only what is short: request is the solve request as it was sent (the answer's inputs), and solution_seal is the seal its answer gave. The request is solved again, under a physics permit and the limits and refusals of solve, and the answer is holds, cause ("solution_seal" when the seal given is not the seal the request solves to), recomputed_solution_seal and recomputed_receipt_sha384 when it holds (else no seal: solve gives the true one), compared, and text_not_compared: no answer text the agent holds is compared. Long form: the whole solve answer sent back as it came, without request. Its solution seal is recomputed from its exact hex values and the part that fails is named, then its request is solved again under a physics permit and the engine's answer compared with it, value by value and byte for byte, receipt included: holds is true only when every byte is the engine's, values_hold when every value is, else cause names the part, solution_seal (the request solves to another seal), answer_text (with differs_at, the first field that differs) or engine_version (an answer of another version). A chained solve: its whole answer with from beside it; the upstream run is computed again and the chain held too (cause chain), with recomputed_chain_seal. Alone it is refused (AnswerCarriesNoRequest). Nothing is stored, so each form answers the same on every connection. On this open connection one address holds at most 1 physics permit at a time, and long work (a solve, a plan of runs or of solves, a run of more than 10000 steps, or a verification that computes one again) runs 1 at a time. A call that finds no permit or no place is answered "Too many concurrent physics tasks." and nothing waits: the same call sent later is answered once one is free. An answer is waited for 60 seconds, and long work is stopped there.

inputSchema.description: Either request and solution_seal alone, the short form: the request is solved again and its seal compared with solution_seal. Or the whole solve answer sent back as it came, without request, the long form: inputs, engine_version, outcome, iterations, reject, result, invariants, field_sha384, seal_parts and solution_seal are then all required. The solution seal is recomputed from its exact hex values and the part that fails is named; then its request is solved again under a physics permit and the limits of solve, and the engine's whole answer to it compared with the answer sent, value by value and then byte for byte, the receipt included, so an answer that holds is every byte the engine's. A seal has no key: an answer whose values were rewritten with its seal parts, seal and receipt worked out again holds every seal, and only the solve shows it is not the engine's (cause solution_seal). The long form's answer carries holds, true when the answer sent is every byte the engine's, and values_hold beside it, true when every value of it is the engine's answer to its request computed again, whatever its spelling: each number by its 64-bit value, strings, flags and null exactly, keys and their order, the receipt string among them. A copy whose numbers a client wrote again in its own spelling (0.0001 for 1.0e-4, 12 for 12.0) has holds false and values_hold true, and differs_at names the first place its text differs. An answer the engine signed (signature, ML-DSA-87 over its receipt, with issued_at, expires_at and nonce) has its signature verified first, against public_key or else this engine's own key: one that does not hold is cause signature, named (SignatureDoesNotVerify, SignatureExpired, SignatureNonceReplayed, SignatureKeyMismatch, ReceiptDoesNotMatch, SignatureAbsent when public_key is given and there is none), and nothing is computed. A signed answer a client wrote again in its own spacing or key order has its signature verified over the receipt it carries; where that receipt does not cover the bytes sent, signature names ReceiptDoesNotMatch with written_again, and the answer is computed again: holds, values_hold and differs_at say what changed.

from.description: Beside the whole answer of a chained solve: the from solve took (request, run_seal, coupling). The upstream run is computed again and held to its seal, each handed value to it, and the request solved again with it; the answer alone is refused (AnswerCarriesNoRequest).

inputs.description: The inputs of the solve answer, sent back as returned: the request that was solved. It is hashed, and solved again under a physics permit and the limits of solve.

public_key.description: The base64 of the ML-DSA-87 public key (2,592 bytes) to verify the answer's signature with; without it, this engine's own.

request.description: With solution_seal alone: the solve request as it was sent (the answer's inputs). It is solved again, under a physics permit and the limits of solve, and its seal is compared with solution_seal. Its fields are solve's. Worked example of the short form, as the whole arguments: {"request":{"solver":"atom_dft","parameters":{"atomic_number":10}},"solution_seal":"<the solution_seal of its solve answer, 96 lowercase hex digits>"}.

seen_nonces.description: Nonces of signatures already seen: one of them again is SignatureNonceReplayed.

solution_seal.description: The solution_seal of the solve answer: with request, or as part of the whole answer.
